summary: The IRAN Act aims to improve the coordination of United States efforts to promote internet freedom and access to information in Iran. It requires updates to federal strategies regarding censorship circumvention tools, establishes Federal Communications Commission considerations for satellite and direct-to-cell communications coverage over Iran, authorizes cybersecurity training and safety tools for Iranian civil society, and authorizes appropriations of $15,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 and 2028.

affected_groups.effect: They may receive enhanced access to secure communications tools, virtual private networks, cybersecurity training, and educational materials regarding regime-controlled applications.
affected_groups.group: Iranian civil society, journalists, and human rights defenders

affected_groups.effect: Must consider encouraging satellite and direct-to-cell communication licensees to avoid geoblocking or degrading coverage over Iran when granting new licenses or market access.
Required to update strategies, submit regular reports and briefings to congressional committees, and manage programs funded by newly authorized appropriations.
affected_groups.group: Department of State and other federal agencies

key_provisions: Amends the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act of 2012 to update strategies for evaluating and increasing access to virtual private networks, decentralized networks, peer-to-peer technologies, and direct-to-cell satellite technologies for Iranian civil society.

Requires the Secretary of State, in consultation with other federal departments, to regularly review and submit updated strategies on digital freedom initiatives in Iran to appropriate congressional committees.

Requires the Federal Communications Commission to consider encouraging licensees and grantees of direct-to-cell or other satellite communications to refrain from intentionally disabling, degrading, or geoblocking coverage of Iran, with specific exceptions.
Requires the Secretary of State to oppose at the International Telecommunication Union any proposal compelling geographic exclusion of Iran from satellite communications coverage.

Directs the Secretary of State to establish or expand programs delivering remote or in-person cybersecurity training, digital safety tools, and multilingual educational materials to journalists, human rights defenders, and civil society actors in Iran.
Authorizes the appropriation of $15,000,000 to the Secretary of State for each of fiscal years 2027 and 2028 to carry out sections relating to satellite safeguards and cybersecurity capacity.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The IRAN Act aims to improve the coordination of United States efforts to promote internet freedom and access to information in Iran. It requires updates to federal strategies regarding censorship circumvention tools, establishes Federal Communications Commission considerations for satellite and direct-to-cell communications coverage over Iran, authorizes cybersecurity training and safety tools for Iranian civil society, and authorizes appropriations of $15,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 and 2028.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs federal strategy and funding toward countering internet blackouts and censorship in Iran by supporting circumvention tools and satellite communications. The financial impact involves authorizing $15,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 and 2028.
